battle.name: 119年的布里甘特人起義
battle.theater: 北英格蘭約克郡谷地與奔寧山麓
battle.brief: 公元119年，不列顛島上號稱全島最強盛的布里甘特部族再度起兵，羅馬不列顛總督昆圖斯·洛利烏斯·烏爾比庫斯率軍入北英格蘭平叛，逐走維努提烏斯並保住附庸女王。卡面希臘重步兵雖未真正踏上英格蘭的戰場，但它代表的盾牆式重步兵邏輯，正是羅馬軍團密集盾陣的源頭。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 公元119年，交戰的兩方是羅馬帝國的中央政權與北不列顛的布里甘特聯盟。羅馬一方是元老院派出的行省總督昆圖斯·洛利烏斯·烏爾比庫斯，麾下是駐紮島上各處的軍團與輔助軍：最靠近戰場的是駐約克（埃博拉庫姆）的第九西班牙軍團，輔助軍以巴達維亞團、西班牙北部與高盧北部的步兵大隊為主，另有騎兵大隊與騎兵中隊負責偵察、追擊與迂回，總督府設於約克，一路經高盧與本土保持聯繫與徵發。布里甘特一方不是一支單一的軍隊，而是由亨伯河以北、泰恩河與提斯河之間的約克郡谷地與奔寧山脈谷地諸部族組成的聯邦式政治體，平日以首長轄下的武裝耕作者與牧戶為骨幹，據點是山間的土木營壘與河谷聚落，沒有常備軍，也沒有統一指揮。布里甘特同時又是羅馬的附庸王國，由女王卡提曼杜娃統治，向羅馬提供兵員、供應與秩序；所以這場起義爆發時，撕開的其實是王國內部：反羅馬的部族首長聯手反抗女王，羅馬介入的目標也從消滅外敵，變成在附庸王國內部扶正一位聽命的女王，再把叛勢壓回去。
countriesEn: The two sides in 119 were the central government of the Roman Empire on one hand and the league of the Brigantes in northern Britain on the other. The Roman side was the senatorial province governor Quintus Lollius Urbicus, with the legions and auxiliaries stationed at various points on the island under him: closest to the fighting was the Ninth Hispana at York (Eboracum), the auxiliaries were chiefly Batavian units and infantry cohorts from northern Spain and northern Gaul, and there were also cavalry alae and cohortes for scouting, pursuit and outflanking, with the governor's headquarters at York and lines of communication and requisition running through Gaul back to Rome. The Brigantes were not a single army but a federal kind of political body made up of the tribes of the Vale of York and the valleys of the Pennines between the Humber in the south and the Tyne and Tees in the north; in peacetime its backbone was the armed cultivators and herdsmen under their own chiefs, its strongholds were earth-and-timber forts in the hills and settlements in the river valleys, and it had no standing army and no unified command. At the same time the Brigantes were also a client kingdom of Rome, ruled by the queen Cartimandua, from whom Rome drew troops, supplies and order; so when this revolt broke out, what actually split open was the interior of the client kingdom. Tribal leaders hostile to Rome joined together to rise against the queen, and the object of Roman intervention changed from destroying an external enemy to putting a compliant queen back on her throne inside the client kingdom and then pushing the rebellion down again.
people: 全場最關鍵的人是布里甘特女王卡提曼杜娃（拉丁文 Cartimanduua），她是羅馬不列顛唯一一位留下名字的本土女王。塔西陀記她與丈夫維努提烏斯成婚，後來這位丈夫反叛，她把丈夫交給羅馬人，羅馬因此把她視為最可靠的附庸，記錄中提到羅馬以金冠與衛兵對待這位女王；傳世僅見一枚刻有她名字的錢幣，是她個人存在的物證。她的兒子同名維努提烏斯（與前夫無關）在母親晚年與她一同向羅馬求援，119年的第二次叛亂中兩人一同退到羅馬一側；卡提曼杜娃死後，兒子維努提烏斯自己成為布里甘特之王，約公元120年再度舉兵，隨即被逐出王國。羅馬方面的核心人物是總督昆圖斯·洛利烏斯·烏爾比庫斯，約公元118至120年間執掌不列顛，據記載他平定布里甘特之亂、驅逐維努提烏斯，並在北部主持修路與設防，是這場戰爭中唯一有明確戰功記錄的羅馬將領。往上一層，上萊茵總督奧盧斯·普拉托里烏斯·涅波斯在118年把羅馬騎兵支隊送往不列顛，那支騎兵是第一次請援時決定王位歸屬的兵力。文字來源只有兩份：普布利烏斯·科爾涅利烏斯·塔西陀的《編年史》與《阿格里科拉傳》，而阿格里科拉正是最早把布里甘特納入羅馬秩序的那位總督；考古方面，萊斯利·阿爾科克自1950年代起主持斯坦威克營壘的發掘，才把這個部族的城防與器物面貌落到實物上。
peopleEn: The decisive figure is the Brigantine queen Cartimandua (Latin Cartimanduua), the only native ruler in Roman Britain whose name has come down to us. Tacitus records that she married a husband named Venutius, that he later rebelled, and that she handed him over to the Romans, which is why Rome treated her as her most reliable dependant; the record has it that Rome honoured this queen with a golden crown and a guard, and only a single coin bearing her name survives, which is the material proof of her existence. Her son, also named Venutius though unrelated to the husband of the same name, petitioned Rome for help together with his mother in her later years, and in the second rising of 119 the two of them withdrew to the Roman side together; after Cartimandua died, her son Venutius became king of the Brigantes in his own right, took up arms again around AD 120, and was promptly driven out of his kingdom. The central Roman figure is the governor Quintus Lollius Urbicus, who held the province of Britain roughly from AD 118 to 120, is credited with ending the Brigantine rising and driving Venutius out, and presided over road building and fortification in the north; he is the only Roman general in this war whose exploits are explicitly recorded. Above him, Aulus Platorius Nepos, legate of Upper Germany, sent a detachment of Roman cavalry to Britain in 118, and that cavalry was the force which decided the succession of the throne at the time of the first petition. There are only two written sources: the Annals and the Agricola of Publius Cornelius Tacitus, and Agricola was the governor who first drew the Brigantes into the Roman order. On the archaeological side, Leslie Alcock began excavating the oppidum at Stanwick in the 1950s, and it is his work that fixed the tribal identity and the material culture of the Brigantes on solid ground.
kits: 卡面是希臘重步兵，這件兵器在公元119年並沒有以原型出現在英格蘭的戰場上：hoplite 方陣是公元前五世紀希臘城邦的產物，到公元二世紀早已被馬其頓長槍方陣取代。因此它在這一役的位置是譜系上的源頭而不是實戰裝備——羅馬軍團用於密集盾陣與縱列推進的連接式大盾，同樣建立在「以盾接盾、以身遮身」的方陣邏輯上；卡面那句「方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽」，說的正是這場衝突中真正決定勝負的東西：把散兵變成一面整體的牆。實戰裝備方面，羅馬一方是步兵的凸面大盾、短劍、重標槍與長矛，以及公元一百年前後開始列裝的分節環形甲與鎖子甲；輔助軍以長盾、短矛、角弓與投槍為主，巴達維亞輔助步兵以泅渡著稱，行軍過河時把盾舉過水面，四世紀兵書韋格蒂烏斯所記的正是這類渡法。布里甘特一方沒有留下被繳獲的清單，但北方不列顛出土的兵器可以說明其樣貌：長矛、投槍、小型圓盾與六角錐形盾、護手狹長的刺擊長劍，以及鎖子甲頭盔。雙方都沒有大型攻城器與攻城砲，攻擊山寨靠的是壕溝、削尖木柵與密集的土木工事，而不是攻城塔。
kitsEn: The card shows a Greek hoplite, and this weapon did not appear on an English battlefield in its original form in AD 119: the hoplite phalanx was a product of the Greek city states of the fifth century BC, and by the second century AD it had long been displaced by the Macedonian pike phalanx. Its place in this campaign is therefore that of an ancestor in the lineage rather than a piece of field equipment. The joined scutum of the Roman legion, used to form the dense testudo and to advance in column, rests on exactly the same logic of shield against shield and body behind body; the line on the card, that the centre of a phalanx is not the individual but the mutual covering, names the thing that really decided this conflict: turning loose men into a single wall. As for the equipment actually in use, the Roman side carried the convex scutum, the gladius, the heavy pilum and the hasta, together with the lorica segmentata and the lorica hamata, the first of which began to be issued around AD 100. The auxiliaries used the long oval shield, the short spear, the bow and the javelin, and the Batavian auxiliaries were famous for swimming rivers fully armed, holding their shields above the water as they crossed; the fourth-century military manual of Vegetius describes exactly this way of fording. The Brigantes left no captured inventory behind, but the weapons excavated in northern Britain show their appearance: spears, javelins, small round shields and hexagonal conical shields, a long thrusting sword with a narrow blade and long point, and mail helmets. Neither side had large siege engines or artillery, and the taking of the hill forts was a matter of ditches, sharpened stakes and dense earthwork defences rather than of towers.
tactics: 羅馬在島上的作戰是典型的不列顛邊疆遠征：總督率主力沿羅馬軍用道路北進，戰役季節集中在春末至初秋，隊伍帶足四到六週的糧秣，宿營設在有水、有圍牆的地方，遇敵則列陣。布里甘特人的抵抗依托山間聚落與河谷地形：他們在奔寧山與約克郡谷地之間的高地據點用土木寨牆固守，寨外以壕溝、削尖木柵和壕溝底的陷阱阻礙接近，一旦羅軍進逼便退入林地與峽谷，游擊騷擾羅軍的糧秣隊與斥候，再用熟悉地形的人手切斷退路。羅馬方面的對策有三：一是先以巴達維亞與西班牙輔助步兵沿用盾牌與身體結成的密集行進隊形頂開地形阻礙，軍團主力在後列陣；二是以騎兵大隊包抄山道與谷口，迫使游擊隊放棄襲擾；三是系統性破壞村莊、穀倉與牲畜，把游擊戰變成饑荒戰，逼叛軍出談判——這是羅馬在北不列顛對付山地部族的老辦法。另一個關鍵是政治操作：羅馬並不打算佔領布里甘特的土地，而是要保留一個聽命的王國，因此戰爭的終點不是屠城，而是讓卡提曼杜娃一系重回王座，再把叛軍首領逐出。
tacticsEn: Roman campaigning on the island was the standard frontier expedition: the governor moved north with the main body along the military roads, the campaigning season ran from late spring to early autumn, the column carried four to six weeks of grain, and the camp was pitched where there was water and a perimeter, the line being formed when contact was made. The Brigantine resistance rested on the hill settlements and the valley terrain: they held the high ground between the Pennines and the Vale of York behind earth-and-timber ramparts, and outside the ramparts ditches, sharpened stakes and pits in the ditch bottoms slowed the approach, while the garrison would fall back into the woodland and gullies as soon as the Roman pressure came on, harassing the baggage train and the pickets, and then cutting the retreat with men who knew the ground. The Roman answer had three parts. First, the Batavian and Spanish auxiliary infantry advanced in a close column, shields and bodies interlocked, to push aside the obstacles of the terrain, with the legion following in formation behind them. Second, the cavalry alae worked round the hill tracks and the mouths of the valleys to pin the guerrillas down and deny them the freedom to strike. Third, the Romans systematically destroyed the villages, the granaries and the cattle, turning a war of harassment into a war of hunger and forcing the rebels to come to terms; this was the old Roman way of dealing with the hill tribes of northern Britain. There was also a political operation running alongside the military one. Rome had no intention of occupying Brigantine territory: it wanted a compliant kingdom kept in being. The end of the war was therefore not the sack of a town but the restoration of Cartimandua's line to the throne and the expulsion of the rebel leaders.
data: 可核對的數字不多，以下只列有根據者。年代方面：布里甘特第二次起義通常定於公元119年；118年那次請援記於塔西陀《編年史》卷十二末，120年前後的叛亂記於卷十三末，烏爾比庫斯執掌不列顛約在公元118至120年之間，當時圖拉真已於公元117年去世、哈德良即位。兵力方面：公元二世紀初不列顛島上常駐約三至四個軍團，另有數十個輔助軍大隊與中隊，輔助軍總人數在萬餘至兩萬的量級；具體到本役，羅馬方面的出動規模沒有留下可信數字，合理的理解是總督自帶一個軍團的分遣隊與若干輔助步兵、騎兵大隊，即以數千人的規模在布里甘特境內作戰。布里甘特方面同樣沒有留下人數，史料只稱其為不列顛島上最強盛的部族，其控制的土地自亨伯河延伸到泰恩河與提斯河，縱深百餘公里，人口在數萬量級。地理方面：作戰區的斯坦威克營壘在卡特里克附近，是不列顛最大的部族營壘之一，面積約三十公頃；羅馬軍用道路自約克向北穿過該區，約克至泰恩河谷約六十公里。錢幣方面：卡特里克一帶出土的錢幣窖藏，1911年一次即達數萬枚，2011年又在同一地點發現數千枚羅馬錢幣，是北英格蘭在公元二世紀初貨幣流通與軍政重心的實證。至於戰損，兩軍的具體死傷與俘虜數字均無可信記載，起義的確切月份也沒有留下記錄，卡面所標的月份取自羅馬作戰季節之中。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and only those with a basis are given here. As to date: the second rising of the Brigantes is usually put in AD 119; the petition of 118 is recorded at the end of Book XII of Tacitus' Annals, the revolt of about AD 120 at the end of Book XIII, and Lollius Urbicus' tenure of Britain fell roughly between AD 118 and 120, at a time when Trajan had died in AD 117 and Hadrian had succeeded him. As to numbers of men: at the beginning of the second century AD some three to four legions were permanently stationed on the island, together with several dozen auxiliary cohorts and cavalry units, the auxiliaries numbering in the region of ten to twenty thousand men; for this campaign in particular no credible figure survives for the size of the Roman deployment, and the reasonable reading is that the governor took a detachment from a legion together with a certain number of auxiliary infantry and cavalry alae, that is, a force of some thousands operating inside Brigantine territory. The Brigantes left no numbers either; the sources only call them the most powerful nation on the island, and the land they controlled ran from the Humber to the Tyne and the Tees, a depth of more than a hundred kilometres, with a population on the order of tens of thousands. As to geography: the oppidum of Stanwick near Catterick lies in the area of operations and is one of the largest tribal oppida in Britain, covering roughly thirty hectares; the Roman military road runs north from York through that area, and the distance from York to the Tyne valley is about sixty kilometres. As to coinage: the hoards found at Catterick include one find of 1911 that numbered tens of thousands of coins, and in 2011 several thousand more Roman coins were turned up at the same spot, evidence for the circulation of money and for the military and administrative weight of northern England in the early second century AD. As to losses: no trustworthy account survives of the dead or the prisoners on either side, and the rising's exact month is likewise unrecorded; the month given on the card is taken from the middle of the Roman campaigning season.
cause: 起義的直接起因在布里甘特王國內部。布里甘特在阿格里科拉時期被納入羅馬的客戶王國體系：女王卡提曼杜娃以割讓地盤、供應兵員、維持地方秩序為代價，換取羅馬的保護與附庸王的地位。但這種體制要求王國內部的敵意必須由王室自己壓住，而布里甘特聯盟並未因此變成一體。羅馬的道路、城鎮、稅收與駐軍不斷深入王國腹地，羅馬的官吏與商人沿軍道向北推進，把原本互不相干的氏族變成彼此競爭的鄰里；年輕人被徵調進輔助軍與軍團，賦役與徵召同時壓在所有人身上，而商品與貨幣的流入又讓首長與首長之間的差距拉開。外部壓力則來自北面：卡爾特人與更北的部落不斷南壓，布里甘特正是前線，王室必須年年出動，兵力和物資年年耗掉。於是一次局部衝突引發全面裂痕：被女王奪去權位的維努提烏斯起兵反叛，黨羽深入王國各地，農莊與穀倉被燒，軍道被切斷。118年第一次請援時，羅馬出兵幫女王守住王位；119年第二次叛亂爆發，叛軍的聲勢超出附庸女王能壓制的範圍，羅馬這才不得不由總督親自率軍介入，把內戰當成對外作戰來打。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the rising lay inside the Brigantine kingdom. The Brigantes had been drawn into the Roman client system during the time of Agricola: the queen Cartimandua paid for Roman protection and the status of a client king with ceded territory, the supply of troops and the keeping of local order. But such a system required the internal enmity of the kingdom to be held down by the royal house itself, and the Brigantine league had not thereby become one thing. Roman roads, towns, taxes and garrisons pushed deeper into the heartland of the kingdom, Roman officials and traders moved north along the military roads, and tribes that had been strangers to one another were turned into competing neighbours; young men were conscripted into the auxiliaries and the legions, taxation and levy fell on everyone at once, and the influx of goods and money widened the distance between chief and chief. The pressure from outside came from the north: the Catuvellauni and the tribes beyond them pushed south without ceasing, the Brigantes stood on the frontier, and the royal house had to take the field year after year, spending men and stores year after year. Then a local quarrel opened the full breach: Venutius, deprived of his position by the queen, rose in revolt, and his partisans spread deep into the kingdom, burning farms and granaries and cutting the military road. When the first petition was made in 118, Rome sent troops to help the queen hold her throne; when the second rebellion broke out in 119, its scale passed what a client queen could contain, and Rome had no choice but to intervene with the governor himself leading the column, treating a civil war as if it were a campaign against a foreign enemy.
impact: 這場起義的直接後果，是北不列顛的附庸體系被重新整理。維努提烏斯被逐出布里甘特，王位回到卡提曼杜娃手中；隨後她死於任內，其子維努提烏斯再度舉兵，約公元120年被烏爾比庫斯第二次平定，之後布里甘特的土地被分割給數位小王，羅馬在約克谷地與奔寧山東麓建立一連串小型堡壘與驛站，烏爾比庫斯主持修築通往北方的主幹道，把羅馬軍道從哈德良長城線一路向北推。更長期的影響有兩條。其一是防禦體制的轉向：從公元一百二三十年代起，不列顛北部的堡壘密度與駐軍規模明顯上升，原本用來監視內部的客戶王國逐步被前沿堡壘網取代，羅馬不再倚賴一位女王維持秩序，而改為直接控制交通線與稅源。其二是軍隊本身的代價：第九西班牙軍團在這幾年裡從編制中消失，此後再未出現；消失的原因至今沒有定論，最常見的說法是它在北進或參與布里甘特戰事時全軍覆沒，但也有學者認為它其實早已在更早的北方遠征中損失殆盡，因此這場起義成了考古學與編年史上的一個長期難題。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the rising was that the client system of northern Britain was put in order again. Venutius was driven out of the Brigantes and the throne returned to Cartimandua; she then died in office, and her son Venutius rose again and was defeated a second time by Urbicus around AD 120, after which the Brigantine territory was divided among a number of lesser kings, Rome raised a chain of small forts and staging posts in the Vale of York and on the eastern slopes of the Pennines, and Urbicus presided over the building of the trunk road running north, carrying the Roman military route from the line of Hadrian's Wall onward into the north. Two effects run longer. The first is the change in the system of defence: from the AD 120s the density of forts and the scale of the garrisons in northern Britain clearly increased, the client kingdom that had been used to police the interior was gradually replaced by a network of forward forts, and Rome no longer relied on a single queen to hold the peace but took direct control of the lines of communication and of the revenue. The second is the cost paid by the army itself: over these same years the Ninth Hispana disappears from the record and never reappears. The reason has never been settled. The commonest explanation is that it was annihilated while campaigning north or in the Brigantine war, but other scholars argue that it had already been all but destroyed in the earlier northern expeditions, and the rising remains a standing problem for archaeology and chronology.
result: 結果可以分三層來看。戰場上：布里甘特叛軍被擊潰，首領被逐出王國，卡提曼杜娃一系保住王位；118年請援時派來的羅馬騎兵與119年總督親率的部隊，兩次決定了王位的歸屬。政治上：布里甘特作為一個獨立的勢力單位從此消失，土地被分割，首長被逐一收編，羅馬在北英格蘭的統治方式也從客戶王國制轉為堡壘與軍道制，帶兵打仗的官職與修路的工程從此成為總督的主要工作。長期上：起義並沒有被徹底消滅，同族同地的叛亂在往後數十年仍不斷出現，羅馬每次都要出兵；布里甘特之名在語源上常被解作「高地者」，與南義大利的布里甘特人同源，其名在後世的凱爾特文獻中亦有流傳。就戰史方法而言，本役留下的教訓是清楚的：遠征的勝負不取決於一次會戰，而取決於能不能在敵人的山區裡維持糧秣線，同時能不能把政治解決方案帶到戰場上。卡提曼杜娃的案子正好說明，只要羅馬願意保留一位附庸女王，附庸體系在一次大規模叛亂之後仍然可以被修復；而她的兒子維努提烏斯在母親死後再度起兵、隨即被逐出，則說明這種修復的代價從來不低。至於本役的確切戰場、確切日期與兵員數字，史料都沒有留下記載，留下來的是兩段記載：塔西陀書中那兩段簡短的報告，以及北方大地裡那些被燒過又被重新住回去的村莊。
resultEn: The result can be read in three layers. On the ground: the Brigantine rebels were broken up, their leaders were driven out of the kingdom, and Cartimandua's line kept the throne; the Roman cavalry sent in response to the petition of 118 and the column led in person by the governor in 119 decided the succession twice over. Politically: the Brigantes ceased to exist as an independent political unit, the land was divided up, the chiefs were absorbed one by one, and the way Rome ruled northern England changed from the client kingdom system to a system of forts and military roads, with the duties of command and road building becoming the governor's principal work. In the longer run: the rising was not stamped out, and revolts in the same country and among the same people continued to break out for decades afterwards, each requiring a Roman expedition; the name of the Brigantes is commonly explained from a root meaning high or elevated, cognate with the Brigantes of southern Italy, and it survives in later Celtic literature. As to method in military history, the lesson of this campaign is plain: the outcome of an expedition is decided not by a single set-piece battle but by whether the grain line can be kept up in the enemy's hills, and whether a political solution can be carried onto the field. The case of Cartimandua shows precisely that, so long as Rome was willing to keep a client queen, the client system could be repaired after a rising on a large scale; and the fact that her son Venutius rose once more after her death and was at once driven out shows that such a repair never came cheap. As for the exact battlefield, the exact dates and the numbers of men, the sources record none of them; what survives is two things: the two brief notices in Tacitus, and the villages of the northern uplands that were burned and then settled again.
